translation.title: Commentary on Sūrat "Tabbat." In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of God, glorified be His praise and hallowed be His names:

Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he (1) His wealth and what he earned did not avail him (2) He will burn in a fire of flame (3) and his wife, the carrier of firewood (4) around her neck a rope of palm fiber (
He, exalted be His mention, says: the hands of Abū Lahab have lost, and he has lost. By His saying
Perish the hands of Abū Lahab
is meant: his work perished. One of the people of Arabic used to say: [continued in the next unit]
Perish the hands of Abū Lahab
is a supplication against him from God. As for
, it is a report. It is mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [b. Masʿūd] it is:
Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and he has perished (

" there indicates that it is a report. This is illustrated by what a speaker says to another: "May God destroy you" as against "He has destroyed you," and "May He make you righteous" as against "He has made you so."
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said about the meaning of
Perish the hands of Abū Lahab
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: Perish the hands of Abū Lahab
: that is, they lost, and he perished.

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said.
m: Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he

is loss. He said: Abū Lahab said to the Prophet ﷺ: "What will I be given, Muḥammad, if I believe in you?" He said: "As the Muslims are given." He said: "Do I have no superiority over them?" He said: "And what do you want?" He said: "Perdition (
) to this religion, perdition, that I should be equal to these!" So God sent down
Perish the hands of Abū Lahab
. He says: because of what their hands did. [Fn 1]

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda.
m: Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he
: he said: the hands of Abū Lahab lost, and he lost. [Fn 2]

x: It was said that this sūra was revealed about Abū Lahab because, when the Prophet ﷺ singled out his clan for the summons, after
[al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:214] was revealed to him and he gathered them for the call, Abū Lahab said to him: "May you perish for the rest of the day! Was it for this that you summoned us?"
Mention of the reports on this:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Abū Muʿāwiya told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: He said: One day the Messenger of God ﷺ ascended al-Ṣafā and said: "Yā ṣabāḥāh!" Quraysh gathered to him and said: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Tell me, if I informed you that the enemy will attack you in the morning or the evening, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abū Lahab said: "May you perish! Was it for this that you called us and gathered us?" So God sent down
Perish the hands of Abū Lahab

c: Abū al-Sāʾib told me, he said: Abū Muʿāwiya told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Numayr told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr b. Murra, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: [al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:214] was revealed, the Messenger of God ﷺ stood on al-Ṣafā and called: "Yā ṣabāḥāh!" The people gathered to him, one man coming and another sending his messenger. He said: "Banū Hāshim, Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, Banū Fihr, O my sons, O my sons: tell me, if I informed you that horsemen at the foot of this mountain wanted [Fn 1] to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abū Lahab said: "May you perish for the rest of the day! Was it for this that you summoned us?" So
Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Abū Usāma told us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr b. Murra, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: He said: When this verse was revealed,

, "and your tribe among them, the sincere ones," the Messenger of God ﷺ went out until he ascended al-Ṣafā and called out: "Yā ṣabāḥāh!" They said: "Who is this who calls?" They said: "Muḥammad." They gathered to him, and he said: "Sons of so-and-so, sons of so-and-so, sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, sons of ʿAbd Manāf." They gathered to him, and he said: "Tell me, if I informed you that horsemen were coming out at the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?" They said: "We have not tried falsehood from you." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abū Lahab said: "May you perish! Did you gather us only for this?" Then he rose, and this sūra was revealed: "
Tabbat yadā Abī Lahabin wa-qad tabba
" ("Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and he has perished"), thus al-Aʿmash recited it, to the end of the sūra. [Fn 3]

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān.
m: Perish the hands of Abū Lahab

, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ sent to him and to others — Abū Lahab was the paternal uncle of the Prophet ﷺ and his name was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā — and reminded them, Abū Lahab said: "May you perish! Was it for this that you sent for us?" So God sent down
Perish the hands of Abū Lahab

evidence.text: It is mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [b. Masʿūd] it is: {Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and he has perished (*wa-qad tabba*)} [Fn 1].
Then he rose, and this sūra was revealed: "*Tabbat yadā Abī Lahabin wa-qad tabba*" ("Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and he has perished"), thus al-Aʿmash recited it, to the end of the sūra.

x: His wealth and what he earned did not avail him
. He, exalted be His mention, says: what did his wealth avail him, and what did it ward off of God's wrath against him?
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: al-Ḥasan b. Dāwūd b. Muḥammad b. al-Munkadir told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Abū al-Ṭufayl.
m: He said: The sons of Abū Lahab came to Ibn ʿAbbās and began to quarrel in the house. Ibn ʿAbbās rose to separate [Fn 1] them, he having lost his sight, and one of them pushed him until he fell onto the bedding. He became angry and said: "Take the filthy earning out from me!" [Fn 2]

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī, from Muḥammad b. Sufyān, from a man of Banū Makhzūm, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: He saw one day some [Fn 3] of the sons of Abū Lahab fighting, and he began to separate them, saying: "These are of what he earned." [Fn 3]

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Layth, from Mujāhid.
m: His wealth and what he earned did not avail him
: he said: what he earned is his children. [Fn 4]

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us. And al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us. Both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.
m: , he said: his children; they are of his earning. [Fn 1]

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.

x: He will burn in a fire of flame
. He, exalted be His mention, says: Abū Lahab will burn in a fire of flame.
and his wife, the carrier of firewood
. He says: Abū Lahab and his wife, the carrier of firewood, will burn in a fire of flame.
. The general body of the reciters of Medina, Kūfa and Basra read it (

) in the nominative [Fn 2], except ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Isḥāq, who read it in the accusative, as has been reported to us from him [Fn 3]. There is a difference about ʿĀṣim, for both the nominative and the accusative are reported from him [Fn 4]. It seems that whoever read it in the nominative made it an attribute of the woman and made what governs the nominative of the woman the preceding predicate,
. It is also possible that what governs it is the description, namely
) as an attribute of the woman. As for the accusative, it is for censure (
). It may also be accusative as a "cutting off" (
) from the woman, because "the woman" is definite and
is indefinite. The correct reading in our view is the nominative [Fn 5], because it is the more eloquent of the two forms, [p. 719] and because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

Some said: she used to bring thorns and throw them on the path of the Messenger of God ﷺ, so that they would enter his foot when he went out to prayer.

m: and his wife, the carrier of firewood

Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid.
Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us. And al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us. Both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.
Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: And his wife, the carrier of firewood
: that is, she used to carry reports from some people to others. [Fn 2]

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda.
m: And his wife, the carrier of firewood

m: And his wife, the carrier of firewood
: he said: she went about with tale-bearing.

x: The more correct of the two views in my opinion is the view of those who said: she used to carry thorns and throw them on the path of the Messenger of God ﷺ, because that is the most apparent meaning of it.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from ʿĪsā b. Yazīd, from Abū [Fn 4] Isḥāq, [sic: "Yazīd Zayd"], who clung to Masrūq more than anything. [The isnād is garbled in the source.]
m: Perish the hands of Abū Lahab
was revealed, it reached the wife of Abū Lahab that the Prophet ﷺ was lampooning her. She said: "For what do they lampoon me? Did you see me, as Muḥammad said, carrying firewood, with a rope of
around my neck?" She waited, then came to him and said: "Your Lord has abandoned you and hated you." So God sent down:
By the morning brightness (1) and the night when it grows still (2) your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He hated you

evidence.text: The reciters differed in reading {*ḥammālata l-ḥaṭab*}.

The general body of the reciters of Medina, Kūfa and Basra read it (*ḥammālatu l-ḥaṭabi*) in the nominative [Fn 2], except ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Isḥāq, who read it in the accusative, as has been reported to us from him [Fn 3].
It seems that whoever read it in the nominative made it an attribute of the woman and made what governs the nominative of the woman the preceding predicate, {will burn}.
The correct reading in our view is the nominative [Fn 5], because it is the more eloquent of the two forms, [p. 719] and because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

notes.ar: ينظر تفسير ابن كثير 8/ 535، وقد أخرج البلاذري في أنساب الأشراف 1/ 139 من طريق آخر عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس مثله.

notes.en: Ibn Abi al-Dunya transmitted it in al-Samt (no. 263) through Sufyan with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في الصمت (263) من طريق سفيان به.

notes.en: Tafsir Mujahid, p. 759. Al-Firyabi transmitted it through Mujahid, as cited in Taghliq al-Taʿliq (4/380). Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/409) to Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Dham al-Ghiba, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 759 ومن طريقه الفريابي - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 380 - وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 409 إلى ابن أبي الدنيا في ذم الغيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/409) to the author and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 409 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted the first part of it in his Tafsir (2/406), up to “by slander,” from Maʿmar with this chain. He transmitted the second part (2/406) from Maʿmar as his statement.
notes.ar: أخرج عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 406 شطره الأول إلى قوله: بالنميمة. عن معمر به. وأخرج شطره الثاني في 2/ 406 عن معمر قوله.

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “Ibn.” He is Abu Ishaq al-Sabiʿi; see his biographical entry in Tahdhib al-Kamal (22/102).
notes.ar: في م: "ابن". وهو أبو إسحاق السبيعي. ينظر ترجمته في تهذيب الكمال 22/ 102.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/409) to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 409 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: His Diwan (2/1341).
notes.ar: ديوانه 2/ 1341.

notes.en: A woman is said to be ʿatalat when she wears no jewelry or adornment and her neck is bare of necklaces. See Lisan al-ʿArab, root ʿ-t-l. The poet is addressing a gazelle, comparing it to his beloved. See his Diwan (2/1342).
notes.ar: عطَلَت المرأة تَعْطَل عَطَلا وعُطولا وتعطَّلت: إذا لم يكن عليها حلى، ولم تلبس الزينة، وخلا جيدها من القلائد. اللسان (ع ط ل). والشاعر يخاطب ظبية يشبهها بمحبوبته. ينظر ديوانه 2/ 1342.

notes.en: T1 reads “from a tree.”
notes.ar: في ت 1: "من شجر".

notes.en: Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Dalaʾil (2/183) through Muhammad ibn Saʿd with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقى في الدلائل 2/ 183 من طريق محمد بن سعد به.

notes.en: T1 reads “al-multaff” (“the twisted”). This gloss does not fit the reports that follow. It appears that the report or reports to which the author’s heading referred have been omitted. This is supported by Ibn Kathir’s statement in his Tafsir (8/536): “Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us; Wakiʿ told us, from Sulaym, the client of al-Shaʿbi, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: ‘Al-masad is palm fiber.’” The heading for the reports the author lists afterward also seems to have been omitted; it may have read: “Others said: al-masad is an iron chain seventy cubits long.”
notes.ar: في ت 1: "الملتف". وهذه الترجمة مخالفة لما سيأتي من الآثار، ويظهر أنه قد سقط الأثر أو الآثار التي ترجم لها المصنف هذه الترجمة، ويشهد لذلك ما قاله ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 536: وقال ابن جرير: حدثنا أبو كريب، حدثنا وكيع، عن سليم مولى الشعبي، عن الشعبي قال: المسد الليف. وكذلك سقطت ترجمة الآثار التي سردها المصنف بعد، وتقديرها: وقال آخرون: المسد سلسلة من حديد طولها سبعون ذراعًا. ذكر من قال ذلك والله أعلم.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/409) to the author, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 409 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم وابن الأنباري في المصاحف.

notes.en: Ibn Hajar mentioned it in Taghliq al-Taʿliq (4/380) from the author.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن حجر في تغليق التعليق 4/ 380 عن المصنف.

notes.en: See Ibn Kathir’s Tafsir (8/536).
notes.ar: ينظر تفسير ابن كثير 8/ 536.

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “the iron bar for the pulley.”
notes.ar: في م: "الحديدة للبكرة".

notes.en: The manuscripts M, T1, T2, and T3 add after it: “He said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah.”
notes.ar: بعده في م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "قال ثنا ابن ثور عن معمر عن قتادة".

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/406), and al-Baladhuri in Ansab al-Ashraf (1/140), through Maʿmar with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 406، والبلاذري في أنساب الأشراف 1/ 140 من طريق معمر به.

notes.en: The two verses appear in Majaz al-Qurʾan (2/315). The first also appears without attribution in Tarikh Dimashq (67/165). The author of Lisan al-ʿArab, root z-h-q, cites them and attributes them to ʿUthman ibn Tariq; the correct attribution is to ʿUmara ibn Tariq, as noted under root m-s-d, where the first verse is cited and attributed to him. Ibn Manzur says Abu ʿUbayda attributed it to ʿUqba al-Hujaymi.
notes.ar: البيتان في مجاز القرآن 2/ 315، والأول منهما في تاريخ دمشق 67/ 165 غير منسوبين. وذكرهما صاحب اللسان (ز هـ ق) ونسبهما إلى عثمان بن طارق، والصواب عمارة بن طارق، كما في مادة (م س د) وذكر هناك البيت الأول ونسبه إليه. قال ابن منظور: وقال أبو عبيدة: هو لعقبة الهجيمي.

notes.en: Amr means “twisted.” Ayanig is the plural of aynaq; aynuq is a plural of naqah (“she-camel”). See Lisan al-ʿArab, roots m-r-r and n-w-q.
notes.ar: أمر: فُتِل. وأيانق: جمع أَيْنق، وأَيْنُق: جمع ناقة. ينظر اللسان (م ر ر، ن و ق).

notes.en: Zahiq means “fleshy and well-filled.” See Lisan al-ʿArab, root z-h-q.
notes.ar: زاهق: سمين ومكتنز. ينظر اللسان (ز هـ ق).

notes.en: His Diwan, p. 129.
notes.ar: ديوانه ص 129.
